ratings.comment: MJ McClure is absolutely brilliant. I wish i could write down every word he said. He's engaging and hilarious. I love his personality and style of teaching. I wish I could take all of his classes. Definitely do the readings. He will notice if you don't reference them in the exams.
Funny, enaging, understanding of & willing to work with disabled students, but does assign a lot of reading (which I didn't do, but other students seemed to take very seriously). Expecting about a C.

He has a great personality but his lectures are sometimes hard to sit through. His tests were also reading heavy, if you don't cite at least one or two articles in your essay responses expect to do poorly on the tests.
Michael Jay McClure is easily one of my favorite professors. Very, very intelligent, and very, very funny. He makes coming to class fun every day. He cares about his students and their success.

So difficult to do the exams.  No matter how much I studied, I could never remember the images you're expected to.  If not for the art I had to memorize I would have gotten a higher grade.  It killed my test grade every time.
Makes art come alive.  extremely knowledgeable

He is passionate but the exams are tough because you need to remember over 200 images, and I think memorizing the exact date was particularly time-consuming and useless that normally other art history courses won't ask. I'll recommend another course for the foundation courses of AH.

McClure's seminar was fantastic. Very challenging material and readings but the discussion is fascinating. The courses pushes you intellectually but receiving a good grade is still easy. Papers are challenging but McClure will give you assistance if you ask. Highly recommend even if you don't have a specific interest in contemporary art.

Best class I've ever taken. Michael Jay is hilarious, and I learned more than I could ever imagine about contemporary art. There are a lot of images to memorize, so don't wait until the last couple of days before the exam or it'll be really tough. If you're looking for an engaging art class I would highly recommend this one.
Best lecture in my college life

Michael J is a great Prof. It's a pain to memorize the paintings but other than that studying for the tests is relatively easy. You do have to work for his class but overall I found it quiet easy. He is distanced from the class, but as a lecturer he is great. Just make sure you have a good TA and you will do well!!

He is a very opinionated teacher. talks to the entire lecture. lots of readings and paintings to memorize. would not recommend either class. had to struggle my way through them because I am an art major.

"Hello my name is Michael Jay McClure, you're sitting at the University of Wisconsin Madison. Welcome to class." You know, not a fan of modern art but this class made me take a second look. He really loves what he does and holds you interest even through the less exciting movements. His exams can be kookidoo zaniness for sure, but it is worth it!

Professor McClure has been my favorite professor during my college career. His lectures are funny and interesting while still being informative. The class isn't the easiest, but he is very clear about what he expects from you, and if you follow his instructions, you will do well.
He is great! Never thought I'd be excited to go to an art history lecture every day. Had him for both 108 and 208 and both are fantastic. I'll miss him next year!

Art 108 with Michael Jay quickly became my favorite class. He is obviously passionate about the material and is always slipping interesting comments and jokes into this lectures, which make the lectures more interesting and easy to follow. I will be genuinely disappointed when I run out of Michael Jay classes to take.

Michael Jay McClure is by far the best professor I've had at Madison. His passion for the material and eloquence in teaching it made the class I was taking merely as a prereq my favorite class. He expects a lot out of his students, but hard work pays off with memorization and engaging in lecture. You'll love it!

I love Michael Jay! He is hands down the best professor I have ever had in my academic career. I enjoyed his class so much that I am looking forward to working with him again in the spring. I have recommended his course to many friends. He is extremely passionate and knowledgeable about art history.

I love Michael Jay.  He is passionate about his subject and it shows.  He takes what might otherwise be a dull subject and makes the class an incredibly enjoyable experience. Yes, he requires his students to memorize a great deal of artwork and to actually read the assigned material, but if you make an effort you will be rewarded w/ a good grade!

McClure is one of the greatest professors I've ever had. Nothing I will ever say in my entire life will amount to the thorough thoughtfulness that is one off-the-fly sentence this man says. He knows the material and is great at communicating it.

He is easily the best professor I have ever had! Both 108 and 208 (which I am in right now) are not easy classes, he always says he teaches it at the same level he would if he was teaching at Harvard. His little jokes and anecdotes definitely help balance the density of the material covered in lecture. If you like Art/Art History, take MJM!

Michael Jay is fab. Memorizing 100 artworks for identification on a test is not. This class is not easy. Tons of memorization; hundreds of pages of dense, difficult articles to read. A lot of work, but a great class anyway. If you like art and art history taking this with MJM is a no-brainer.
Michael Jay is a phenomenal instructor!  His lecture was always the highlight of my academic day.  He does a great job keeping your attention and explaining even the most difficult topic.

He is probably the funniest teacher I have ever had. His lectures are very thorough and deep, so the humour helps balance it out and keep it fresh. He talks very fast and uses very fancy sounding words, but will almost always define them as he's speaking. The tests are difficult if you haven't studied, and pretty easy if you have.
Hilarious. Makes lecture entertaining.  If you must take Foundations of Contemporary Art you MUST take it with him. Probably the best professor I have ever had.

michael jay is fantastic. he was hilarious and incredibly into what he taught. i had him for art 108, which i was told was an easy entry level class. however, i was one of the few freshman in the class. the readings could be difficult but were extremely helpful in 108 and other classes. my TA did a great job of breaking them down for our section.

Michael J. is a great professor.  Even if your not interested in art history (as I wasn't) he makes the class very entertaining and is extremely funny. I had him for 108 and 208.  Still expect to do a lot of studying and memorization for the tests though.

Makes even the most difficult art concepts easy to understand. I've learned more in this course about contemporary art than ever before. He's interesting and hilarious! Favorite lecture at Madison so far.
Extremely intelligent and witty.  Classes were enjoyable, informative, and challenging.  Easily one of the best courses I have taken.

Michael Jay is hilarious. With catch phrases like "What the HELLo Kitty are you talking about, Michael Jay?" and "Wackadoo" this professor will keep you entertained. Lectures FLY by: you're so busy writing and laughing you don't want it to end.

Michael Jay is FABULOUS! I learned a lot in both classes I took with him. He brings a lot of energy & humor into the lectures, and explains things multiple times in different ways. The exams are very difficult - 4 essay questions and 7 image identifications (but you have to memorize 150+) but it is worth it. Lectures were very enjoyable.
Great

Michael J. is my favorite professor at Madison so far. There is a lot of reading but he makes it super interesting. He is absolutely hilarious! I didn't even want to take the class but my first day of lecture I totally changed my mind. Awesome prof.

I took 108 my first semester and then 208 just for fun the next. His lectures were everything I wanted from an Art History lecture plus the added bonus of pop culture references left and right. His exams are hard, don't be fooled, but you'll get what you give. Thinking out of the box and READING the MATERIAL is necessary.

Michael Jay is awesome. He makes class enjoyable. All the lectures are interesting, but the class is very hard. Lots of articles to read. 3 tests (non-cumulative) include 4 essays and 7 identifications (but you have to memorize over 200 images for these IDs). It's hard, but this class is awesome.
One of the most fun teachers you will ever have. Take his art history classes. They're hilarious.
M.J. is like a rock star on stage. He excites his audience during every class period. You can tell he loves to teach. I miss this class.

Super funny, really smart.  Won't win any prizes for cultural sensitivity.  It's white, straight artists for much of the show and MJ loves that. Makes inappropriate comments about Others.  He's funny though and a total diva.
Easy-Medium class. Depends on the TA if you have homework due every week. mandatory attendance but he is really funny and animated. i would recommend this class for sure. 3 non cumulative tests.

The class was really cool most of the time. He tells funny jokes during most classes, and we looked at lots of cool/interesting art. You learn a lot about modernism, even in a historical sense for non-art majors, but it's VERY European-centered. Try to get Paul Prindle for your TA, he's great.
He's funny, very intelligent, and engaging.  The class may be mandatory, but it's not torture (at all) to sit through.  Definitely not the cliche dry/boring art prof.
super funny...my favorite class this semester

Well, first off he is freakin hilarious. He comes out of no where with one liners you share with your friends. The information was clear. Lots of reading of which I didn't do a whole lot of...but didn't do too bad on the exams. I recommend this class, but there is a lot of memorization of art works.
i want to be his best friend. micheal jay is hilarious. his class is by far my favorite. he constantly talks to himself and has ridiculous hand gestures that always make class exciting.
michael jay is witty, fun, and extremely entertaining.  the lectures and discussions are interesting and engaging and i would recommend his class to anyone.
